review_scope: Final read-only lesson QA after prose fixes and embed landing; only this report was authored.

summary.reason: The lesson is mathematically sound, substantial, coherent, and unusually strong in its convention audits and exercises. It is not ready for reviewed because the required interactive task becomes visually unusable in dark theme: preset button labels inherit the browser button color rather than the theme ink color and render nearly black on a dark panel. The raw DTFT/DFT SVG also scales several load-bearing mobile labels to roughly 6 CSS pixels, and two component figures create nested figure elements inside the MDX Figure wrapper.

sources_and_context_read: All 13 JSON artifacts already present in the target lesson-cycle directory
All four figure implementations/assets, the PaddingVsDataLab implementation, and both registries

render_and_interaction_evidence.lesson_preview: npm run preview -- digital-signal-processing dft-bins-symmetry-and-scaling completed and produced light/dark chapter and figure sheets.
render_and_interaction_evidence.desktop_light_dark: DftBasisCorrelations, dtft-dft-bin-samples, RealDftConventionLedger, and PaddingDurationResolution were visually inspected in both themes; plots, equations, cell ledgers, and semantic colors are unclipped and numerically consistent.
render_and_interaction_evidence.mobile_light_dark: All four visuals were inspected at 360–390 CSS px. Component figures reflow without horizontal clipping. The raw 640-wide SVG shrinks 11–13 viewBox-unit labels to about 5.6–6.7 CSS px, below comfortable legibility.
render_and_interaction_evidence.demo_initial_state: Padded pair starts alive at N=64, Q=16, L=1024 and reports: 'FAIL. pair φ=0° · live peaks 171.00 Hz · two-phase FAIL' with a 1.00 Hz displayed grid.
demo_guided_task: Coarse tone followed by two keyboard ArrowRight changes reaches Q=4 and reports 'PASS. single 173 Hz · f̂=172.00 Hz · e_bin=0.0625'.
Padded pair reports phase-test peaks 171.00 Hz versus 166.00/187.00 Hz and remains FAIL at L=1024.
Long pair holds L=1024 and the 1.00 Hz grid, increases acquisition to N=256/250.0 ms, and reports two-phase PASS with peaks at 170.00 and 180.00 Hz in both tests.
render_and_interaction_evidence.dark_theme_defect: At 390 px dark theme, the four scenario labels and the two phase-preset labels are effectively black on the #1d1d1b panel. components/ui/Button.tsx supplies border/background classes but no theme-aware text class, so the native button text color does not inherit var(--ink).
render_and_interaction_evidence.semantic_markup_defect: The preview reports six figure elements for four authored figure embeds because RealDftConventionLedger and PaddingDurationResolution return <figure> inside the outer components/mdx/Figure.tsx <figure>; this is invalid nested figure markup and weakens caption semantics.

checks: For x=[1,0,-1,0], the raw N=4 DFT is [0,2,0,2], and the inverse check at n=2 returns -1; the paired body problem x=[1,0,1,0] correctly gives [2,0,2,0].
The signed half-open maps are correct: N=8, f_s=8 kHz gives [0,+1,+2,+3,-4,-3,-2,-1] kHz, and N=6, f_s=12 kHz gives [0,+2,+4,-6,-4,-2] kHz with one Nyquist singleton.
For a real input, X[(N-k) mod N]=X*[k]; DC and even-N Nyquist are real, while odd N has no Nyquist singleton.
The phased and composite cosine coefficients are correct: 4e^{±jπ/3} for the shifted unit cosine and {16,12e^{-jπ/4},8,12e^{jπ/4}} at bins {0,2,4,6} for the composite record.

The scale family is internally consistent: αβN=1; the alternating N=8 record has raw, unitary, and forward-scaled magnitudes 8, √8, and 1; Parseval's factor is 1/N for the course pair and 1/(N|α|²) generally.
The convolution examples are correct: [1,1,-2] wraps to [-1,1] at N=2; [1,3,5,3] wraps to [4,3,5] at N=3; [2,5,1,-2] wraps to [0,5,1] at N=3; N≥L_x+L_h-1 is the safe allocated-length condition.
The off-bin N=8 cosine coefficients quoted to six decimals are correct and nonzero in all bins, with the stated conjugate pairs.
The padding lab numbers are reproduced by the running implementation: 0.1875 original bins at Q=1, 0.0625 at Q=4, padded-pair failure at N=64/L=1024, and long-pair success at N=256/L=1024.
The forward exercise correctly derives X[k]=E[k]+W_8^kO[k] and X[k+4]=E[k]-W_8^kO[k] from four-periodic E,O and W_8^{k+4}=-W_8^k.

exercise_audit.parallel_pair: The worked x=[1,0,-1,0] row audit is followed immediately by x=[1,0,1,0] using the same basis-row method.
exercise_audit.earlier_concept_required: Closing Exercise 3 cannot be solved as intended without the prerequisite's finite-record DTFT model; its solution explicitly recalls that model with a Ref.
exercise_audit.forward_evidence: Only closing Exercise 6 derives even/odd reuse and ends with '<Ref lesson="fft-factorization-and-layout">FFT Factorization and Machine Layout</Ref> formalizes this reuse recursively as the radix-two FFT'.

rubric.criterion: Opening precisely states the problem in declarative sentences
rubric.evidence: 'The DFT samples one period of a finite record’s spectrum and therefore inherits both periodic indexing and implementation conventions.' The opening is verbatim from course.yaml and contains no question or tease.

rubric.criterion: Concrete instance precedes formalism
rubric.evidence: Before the Definition, the lesson reuses 'x[n]=cos(2π(2/8)n)' and '[X[0],…,X[7]]=[0,0,4,0,0,0,4,0]' from the predecessor.

rubric.criterion: Everything serves the single stated goal
rubric.evidence: The six promised moves are 'declare the transform, attach units to its bins, exploit real symmetry…, audit scale, distinguish circular from linear convolution, and separate denser spectral sampling from longer observation'; each is part of computing or interpreting the finite DFT contract.

rubric.criterion: Chapter is substantial
rubric.evidence: The chapter derives inversion, real conjugacy, Parseval, and circular convolution; audits even/odd endpoints and three scale conventions; and tests padding against acquired duration across ten solved problems.

rubric.criterion: Environments are honest and hypotheses explicit
rubric.evidence: The repaired theorem now begins 'For a positive integer N and integers k and ℓ'; both the roots-of-unity and circular-convolution theorems contain real proofs, and both definitions include canonical, different-surface, boundary, and near-miss cases.

rubric.criterion: Most exercises require production in mathematics and include a parallel problem
rubric.evidence: The set requires computation, boundary analysis, refutation, derivation, representation choice, and factorization; the immediate '[1,0,1,0]' problem is parallel to the worked '[1,0,-1,0]' audit.

rubric.criterion: Earlier concepts are required and confusable types are mixed
rubric.evidence: Closing Exercise 3 requires the earlier finite-record DTFT, while Exercise 5 asks the learner to choose between 'phase-sensitive reconstruction' and 'reporting tone amplitude' without naming the representation in advance.

rubric.criterion: Every solution shows a complete path and no trick questions
rubric.evidence: All ten Exercises contain Solutions with equations, convention decisions, checks, and interpretations; for example the circular problem computes four linear samples, performs the modulo wrap, and derives the minimum N.

rubric.criterion: At most one mechanical closing exercise
rubric.evidence: Only closing Exercise 1 is a direct DFT/inverse audit; Exercises 2–6 probe boundaries, refute, derive, choose a representation, or discover factorization.

rubric.criterion: At least two difficulty-floor archetypes
rubric.evidence: The closing set includes a boundary probe, a false claim to refute, a skipped derivation, and a strategy-choice problem.

rubric.criterion: Exactly one forward closing exercise with Ref
rubric.evidence: Only closing Exercise 6 reaches forward, and its solution explicitly links 'FFT Factorization and Machine Layout'.

rubric.criterion: Callouts pass the deletion test
rubric.evidence: The retrieval Aside supplies otherwise absent feedback; the convolution KeyFact now preserves the keeper contrast 'N=2 periodic indexing gives [-1,1], while padding…N=3 preserves [1,1,-2]'.

rubric.criterion: No citation appears for its own sake
rubric.evidence: Body references are continuity links such as 'DTFT and Frequency Response established…'; secondary surveys appear only in References.

rubric.criterion: No narration of the obvious or flavor idiom
rubric.evidence: Solution lead-ins such as 'The strategy is to compute the full linear output first, then reduce its indices modulo…' name actual mathematical decisions.

rubric.criterion: Each visual carries an idea and remains usable
rubric.evidence: The captions state claims ('Padding samples the same finite-record spectrum more densely…'), and all four visuals carry distinct ideas, but the 640-wide raw SVG scales load-bearing 11–13-unit labels to roughly 6 CSS px at 360 px. Two component visuals also nest their own <figure> inside the MDX <Figure> wrapper.

rubric.criterion: Demo reveals dynamic behavior, starts alive, and supports the stated task
rubric.evidence: The lab numerically fulfills 'Use the four presets in order' and starts at an informative FAIL, but in dark theme the named preset labels are nearly black on the dark panel. A learner cannot visually identify the required presets, so the prose task is not reliably achievable in a supported theme.

rubric.criterion: Cadence and section subdivision
rubric.evidence: No sampled run exceeds three prose paragraphs without a heading, environment, callout, table, or figure; long sections are split by descriptive ### headings such as 'Storage and amplitude reporting solve different problems'.

rubric.criterion: Fold-stripped skeleton reconstructs the argument
rubric.evidence: The skeleton reads 'Eight correlations become one declared transform' → 'A bin acquires hertz only from N and the sample rate' → 'Real records halve storage, not the transform' → 'Scaling is an interface contract' → 'DFT multiplication wraps the convolution' → 'More plotted bins do not add observation'.

rubric.criterion: Typed emphasis and em-dash discipline
rubric.evidence: Bold marks the defined payoff terms 'acquisition aperture' and 'circular convolution'; italics marks first-use 'one-sided peak-amplitude spectrum'; inline code marks the literal token 'fftshift'; only four em dashes occur in the whole lesson.

rubric.criterion: Dry engineering register
rubric.evidence: Declaratives such as 'High array indices therefore do not mean high positive physical frequencies' carry the argument; no rhetorical questions, teases, invented personas, exclamations, or chatty asides occur.

rubric.criterion: References are real, relevant, and chapter-precise
rubric.evidence: The four entries route to Oppenheim–Schafer §§8.4–8.7/10.1–10.2, Lyons §§3.1–3.14, MIT Sessions 17–18, and Schaedler Lessons 15/21–25/28, with the MIT normalization translation stated explicitly.

rubric.criterion: Lessons 1–2 are the gentlest polished entry
rubric.evidence: Single-lesson review of course lesson 8; whole-course entry polish was not scored.

rubric.criterion: Whole-course spiral coverage
rubric.evidence: Single-lesson review; whole-course spiral coverage was not scored.

rubric.criterion: Whole-course scope, outcomes, and technical titles
rubric.evidence: Single-lesson review; only the target lesson's goal/spine alignment was assessed.

rubric.criterion: Paragraph after opening places the move in the course argument
rubric.evidence: It explicitly says Sampling ended with eight correlations, DTFT established the continuous periodic function, and 'This lesson turns those values into a complete finite coordinate system'.

rubric.criterion: Section seams chain the running question
rubric.evidence: Sampled seams open from unresolved prior facts: 'The coefficient index becomes a frequency coordinate only after…', 'The negative-frequency half is redundant…, but…', and 'The continuous DTFT theorem maps linear convolution…, but…'.

rubric.criterion: Last content section hands off consistently with the spine
rubric.evidence: The closing inventories the complete coefficient contract and says the FFT lesson 'exploits repeated roots of unity to compute exactly these coefficients with fewer operations'.

rubric.criterion: Headings carry claims where possible
rubric.evidence: 'Real records halve storage, not the transform', 'Scaling is an interface contract', and 'More plotted bins do not add observation' are claim headings rather than topic labels.

rubric.criterion: Two sampled body sections pass the cover test
rubric.evidence: Without their seam and last sentences, the scale body still derives αβN=1 and Parseval; the padding body still controls N versus L and computes the phase-stability comparison.

rubric.criterion: Immediate predecessor closing joins the opening
rubric.evidence: The predecessor ends with '[0,0,4,0,0,0,4,0]' and promises 'indexing, physical hertz labels, normalization, symmetry, and circular interpretation'; the target opens by inheriting precisely those eight correlations and declarations.

rubric.criterion: No mid-prose secondary-survey attribution
rubric.evidence: No sentence says a textbook 'describes' the material; named external works remain in the final References block.

rubric.criterion: Places and events are anchored
rubric.evidence: No geographic places or historical events occur in this mathematics lesson.

rubric.criterion: Named-term load is controlled
rubric.evidence: New terms arrive in separate beats: DFT pair, signed bin map, one-sided amplitude report, normalization, circular convolution, then zero padding.

rubric.criterion: Earlier material is recalled with Ref and reminder
rubric.evidence: The opening Ref clauses remind the reader what Sampling and DTFT established, and the convolution section recalls 'zero-extended linear convolution' with a Ref before using it.

rubric.criterion: Numeric prose carries its frame
rubric.evidence: Examples state N, f_s, units, denominators, phase sets, or consequences in the same sentence, such as 'f_s=1024 samples/s…N=64…spacing 16 Hz'.

rubric.criterion: Keeper numbers are identifiable and live in callouts/figures
rubric.evidence: The N=8 coefficient audits are visible in the basis/DTFT ledgers, while the revised convolution KeyFact preserves the compact '[-1,1]' versus '[1,1,-2]' boundary result.

rubric.criterion: No data-row narration of human events
rubric.evidence: No human-event evidence occurs.

rubric.criterion: Body details pass the deletion test
rubric.evidence: The 3/16 and 1/16 errors drive the lab target; the 0°/90° perturbation tests stability; N=64/256 isolates duration; and the N=2/3 wrap drives the boundary inference.

rubric.criterion: Sourced rasters pass visible-not-legible
rubric.evidence: The lesson uses no sourced raster images.

rubric.criterion: Real misconceptions are explicitly refuted
rubric.evidence: The lesson replaces bins-as-physical-tone-detectors with finite-record DTFT sampling and replaces padding-as-resolution with the controlled distinction between transform length L and acquired length N.

rubric.criterion: Importance is marked by device shift, not intensifiers
rubric.evidence: Definitions, Theorems, Examples, Tasks, Aside, KeyFacts, and Exercises retain distinct roles; no adjective or intensifier is used as a substitute for structure.

prioritized_fixes.change: Add an explicit theme-aware text color (for example text-ink) to the shared Button base classes, then rerender PaddingVsDataLab in dark desktop and dark mobile. The preset names must remain plainly visible in active and inactive states.

Provide a mobile composition that keeps the axis, k row, X[4]=8, and hertz ledger at readable CSS size; stacking the plot and ledger or converting this to a responsive component figure is preferable to shrinking the 640-wide canvas.
Return a neutral div/section root rather than figure, and replace the internal figcaption with a non-caption summary so components/mdx/Figure.tsx remains the sole figure/figcaption owner.

manual_spot_check_after_fixes: At 390 px in dark theme, read every scenario and phase-preset label before and after selection, then keyboard-run Coarse tone → Q=4 → Padded pair → Long pair.
At 360 px in both themes, verify that every raw DTFT/DFT figure label is comfortably readable without zoom and that all eight bin markers remain distinguishable.
Inspect the rendered DOM: four authored Figure embeds should yield four non-nested figure elements, each with one correctly associated outer caption.
